AWS Bedrock LLM

AWS Bedrock offers a very simple deployment service of full state of the art un-quantized foundational LLMs for you to run on your AWS account. While these models and their data should be private to your account each model does have its own EULA and can vary from model to model.

Connecting to AWS Bedrock

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM
️💡

Valid account setup required!

You must have a valid AWS Account (opens in a new tab) to use AWS Bedrock -

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM use AWS Bedrock - this service is not free.

You must be an administrator or root user of the account to follow the below steps. Otherwise, consult with your account admin.

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM

Obtain IAM credentials to use for Bedrock

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM

Heads up! You can optionally use

metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM you do not want to create a new IAM user. Both forms of authentication are supported for AnythingLLM's AWS Bedrock integration. Learn more about temporary session tokens on AWS → (opens in a new tab)

the following below is for using IAM user authentication. If you are using session tokens this section is not relevant.

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM
🚫

Do not use your root AWS access ID and Key for Bedrock. You should always use the least privileged policy possible when using AWS keys in any third-party applications, not just AnythingLLM.

Ideally, you should create a new user with at least the following permission and policy below. The below policy

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM does not limit access to any particular model, but is good for starting. It is up to you to modify the access level of whatever credentials will be used with AWS Bedrock depending on your use-case.

The below credentials allow a user to see models and stream responses as well as default synchronous response - which is used for @agents.

Copy the desired model you wish to use.

metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM
️💡

Please only use a chat capable model for LLM selection. Incompatible model types will not produce chats in AnythingLLM.

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM

All models on Bedrock require permission from the model owner for use on your AWS account. Access is usually granted very quickly. You can request model permission from a link like this (replace us-west-2 with you region) https://us-west-2.console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/home?region=us-west-2#/modelaccess (opens in a new tab)

metadata.title: aws-bedrock.html
metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM

Now that you have set up and have AWS Bedrock ready for LLM chatting, you can input the credentials to AnythingLLM.

metadata.text:

AWS Bedrock Session Token

This is the session token of the user who can invoke models on Bedrock. You must be using temporary session tokens to use this and have selected the Session Token form of authentication in the UI. The default form of authentication is using IAM user credentials.

metadata.docSource: a text file uploaded by the user.
metadata.text:
sourceDocument: aws-bedrock.html published: 7/4/2025, 5:46:47 PM

AWS region

This is the region that your account is enabled to use with AWS Bedrock - this depends on your region preference and account settings. An example is us-west-2 Oregon. Yours may be elsewhere.

This is the maximum amount of tokens that can exist in a single query for a model. This is a model specific parameter and will vary from model to model.
